task_instance: Attempt a basic bounded Win32 debug-output capture: run `dbgviewcli --no-banner --duration 10` to capture OutputDebugString output from a small test program, or at minimum check `dbgviewcli --status`.
blocker_detail: The skill's entire core deliverable requires the Windows OS: `dbgviewcli.exe` is a native Windows PE binary that reads OutputDebugString via the Win32 DBWIN shared-memory/mutex mechanism and, for kernel capture, loads a kernel-mode driver (Dbgv.sys); boot logging writes Windows registry keys; and the skill's own security rule requires verifying the binary's Authenticode signature with `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` (PowerShell on Windows). This runtime is Linux x86_64 (uname -a: 'Linux vm 6.18.44-fc-v37 ... x86_64 GNU/Linux') with no Windows kernel, no Win32 subsystem, and no Wine installed (checked `which wine` -> not found). There is no way to produce or capture real OutputDebugString/DbgPrint output, load a Windows kernel driver, or run a Windows PE executable in this environment. This is not a missing package that could be installed (like apt-get); it is an OS-level capability (Windows kernel/Win32 debug-output plumbing) absent from the runtime by design, so no partial or simulated attempt would exercise the actual skill.
evidence: Ran `uname -a` inside the work directory, confirming Linux x86_64 kernel with no Windows/WSL/Wine layer. Ran `which wine` with no result, confirming no Windows-binary compatibility layer is available either. No dbgviewcli.exe binary exists or can exist to run in this environment; the skill document (benchmark/ce_sources/microsoft__skills__debugview/SKILL.md) explicitly scopes the tool to 'Windows Vista or later (x64, ARM64)' and requires kernel driver loading, registry access, and PowerShell Authenticode verification, none of which are possible on Linux.
